title: Customer-level change explainer and signal decomposition for usage/cost/latency anomalies
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Objective: Build a service and pipeline stage that produces concise, human-readable explanations for detected anomalies in customer usage/cost/latency metrics. The goal is to reduce wakeups for on-call, speed triage for customers and SEs, and enable automated suppression for explained noise.

Background: We have multiple anomaly detectors producing alerts across usage, cost, and latency (streaming and batch). Current alerts often lack actionable context: which customer attributes, routes, or query patterns drove the change, and whether the delta is driven by traffic shifts, model changes, or billing accounting artifacts. This ticket implements an explainability/decomposition layer that consumes candidate anomalies and emits an "explanation payload" attached to alerts and stored in console timelines.

Scope & constraints:
- Input: candidate anomaly events (time window, metric, entity/customer id, severity) from the anomaly pipeline (streaming Kafka topic and batch historical store).
- Output: structured explanation summary (plain-text summary, top-3 contributing dimensions, percent attribution, likely root causes, suggested next steps, confidence score). Output will be string fields in alert payloads and saved to the console events DB.
- Must be performant: 95th percentile explanation generation latency < 3s for streaming alerts and < 60s for high-volume group aggregation jobs.
- Must not affect the anomaly decision signal: explanation is derived post-detection.
- Must support retroactive recomputation (for explanation improvements) and versioned explanation schemas.

Proposed approach:
1) Decomposition engine: hybrid method combining fast heuristics + attribution for top categorical/time dimensions (route, model_version, region, token_buckets, plan_tier) and a lightweight attribution model inspired by SHAP for aggregated metrics. Use historical baselines (rolling 7d/28d) and compare expected vs observed counts and mean latencies.
2) Attribution steps: compute delta by dimension using pre-aggregated group-by counts from our OLAP store (day/hour granularity). Rank by absolute contribution and normalize to percent of total delta. Identify whether delta is volume-driven, per-request-latency-driven, or price-change-driven (billing tag changes).
3) Explainability text generator: template-based natural language summaries (for alerts and timeline) plus an optional short bullet list for automated emails and Slack messages. Templates parameterized by top contributors and confidence.
4) Suppression & runbook links: if explanation matches known benign patterns (scheduled backup traffic, batch job labels, known usage spike driver list), mark alert as "info" or suggest suppression rules to SRE/PM.
5) Storage and API: store explanation artifacts in console-events table (explanation_v=1) and surface via console backend endpoint /v1/alerts/:id/explanation. Include a compact JSON-safe string that will be included in existing alert payloads sent to PagerDuty/Slack.

Success metrics:
- 25% reduction in number of P1/P2 calls attributable to explained alerts within 8 weeks of rollout.
- 40% faster median triage time for explained anomalies (time from alert to triage comment).
- Explainability coverage >= 90% of streaming anomalies and >= 95% of batch anomalies where required aggregates exist.

Out-of-scope: automatic remediation, full ML-model explanations (we'll start with heuristics + lightweight attribution, then iterate).
acceptance_criteria: Explanation artifacts stored and versioned in console-events with stable schema (explanation_v=1)
Console backend endpoint /v1/alerts/:id/explanation returns human-readable summary and top contributors within 3s for streaming alerts
Explanation included in alert payload sent to Slack/PagerDuty (compact, <1KB) when enabled
Dashboard panel in console-2026.03 release shows percent attribution breakdown per example alert and aggregated coverage metrics
Runbook updated with suppression suggestions and how-to for SEs (link included in comments)
comments: 2026-02-11 - Kickoff: scoped scope with PM (Luis Ortega) and Design (Maya Patel). Decided to start with template-driven summaries and a deterministic attribution method to avoid model drift risk.

2026-02-16 - Data discovery: confirmed required group-bys exist in OLAP (hourly by customer_id, route, model_version, region, plan_tier). Need to add token_bucket dimension to hourly aggregates (follow-up ENG-35856).
2026-02-22 - Design sync: UX wants two summary lengths: short (one sentence) for Slack and long (3-4 bullets) for console timeline. Added acceptance criteria for both formats.

2026-02-28 - Implementation started: added a new microservice module explain-decomposer under console-backend (branch: github.com/redwood-inference/console-backend/tree/feature/ENG-35840-explain-decomposer).

2026-03-03 - Prototype: local benchmark shows mean explanation latency 1.8s for single-customer streaming events against cached hourly aggregates. Need memory tuning for warm cache hit-rate. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-backend/pull/2234 (WIP).

2026-03-05 - Security review kickoff scheduled 2026-03-07 (explanations may surface PII via route names and customer labels). Threat model: ensure masking rules for sensitive labels and opt-out per customer (privacy compliance).
2026-03-05 - Next steps: finalize suppression heuristics list with SRE, add unit tests for explanation stability, and schedule canary rollout to 10% of alerts for two internal customers.
